question: What personalised gene-editing treatment did baby KJ Muldoon receive, as reported in 2025?
text:
Baby KJ Muldoon received **k-abe (kayjayguran abengcemeran)**, a personalised **CRISPR adenine base-editing therapy** designed to correct a specific mutation in his *CPS1* gene. The treatment was infused intravenously, using lipid nanoparticles to deliver the editor to his liver cells. His first infusion was on February 25, 2025. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12713542/))

KJ was born with severe **carbamoyl phosphate synthetase 1 (CPS1) deficiency**, a rare disorder that prevents the body from clearing toxic ammonia effectively. The May 2025 report found that after treatment he could tolerate more dietary protein and needed less ammonia-lowering medication, though longer follow-up was needed. ([beta.nih.gov](https://beta.nih.gov/news-events/nih-research-matters/infant-rare-disease-receives-customized-gene-therapy?utm_source=openai))
